qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Lecture twelve. Particle swarm optimisation. This is how a swarm of simple guesses finds the best spot.
Each blue dot is a particle, one guess at the answer.
Each dot is a particle: one guess at the answer.
Its guess is a position, two numbers on the map. This one is at six point four, five point eight.
Its guess is a position: two numbers on the map.
The odour where it stands is its fitness. Here that is eleven.
The odour where it stands is its fitness.
Each particle also has a velocity, a small grey arrow. It is the next move.
Each particle also has a velocity: its next move.
Now the map fades. No particle can see it, only the odour underfoot.
No particle sees the map, only the odour underfoot.
To move, a particle adds its velocity to its position.
To move, a particle adds its velocity to its position.
The position three, five, plus the velocity two, minus one, lands on five, four.
With c one and c two at zero, there are no pulls. Every dot flies straight on.
With no pulls, every dot just flies straight on.
Nothing steers them towards the scent, so no dot finds the food.
Nothing steers them towards the scent.
Now follow one particle for a single step.
Follow one particle for one step.
The grey arrow is the velocity it already has.
Grey: the velocity it already has.
The purple arrow pulls it towards its own best spot so far, called p.
Purple: a pull towards its own best spot, p.
The orange arrow pulls it towards the swarm's best spot, called g.
Orange: a pull towards the swarm's best spot, g.
Head to tail, the three arrows make the new velocity, and the particle moves.
Added head to tail, they make the new velocity.
Its new odour, twenty-five, does not beat fifty-two. So p stays where it was.
Its new odour, 25, does not beat 52, so p stays.
The same sum in one dimension. The particle is at four, its best at seven, the swarm's best at two.
One dimension: x is 4, its best 7, the swarm's 2.
c one and c two set how hard each pull is. z one and z two are random, between zero and one.
c₁, c₂ set how hard; z₁, z₂ are random draws.
First, it keeps its velocity of one.
It keeps its velocity of 1.
Two times a half times seven minus four. The pull to its own best adds three.
The pull to its own best adds 3.
Two times a half times two minus four. The pull to the swarm's best adds minus two.
The pull to the swarm's best adds minus 2.
So the new velocity is two, and the particle moves from four to six.
New velocity 2, so it moves from 4 to 6.
z one and z two are drawn fresh at every step.
z₁ and z₂ are fresh random numbers every step.
Roll again, and the same particle lands somewhere else.
Roll again and the same particle lands elsewhere.
Each hollow dot is one possible landing spot.
Each hollow dot is one possible landing spot.
This spread stops the swarm settling too soon.
This spread stops the swarm settling too soon.
Now all fourteen particles take that step together.
All 14 particles take that step together.
The swarm's best odour climbed. Sixty-six, seventy-eight, eighty-five, then ninety-nine.
The swarm's best climbed: 66, 78, 85, then 99.
Pulled to their own bests and the swarm's, they gather.
Pulled to their own bests and the swarm's, they gather.
They circle the food and keep searching.
They swarm around the food and keep searching.
Nobody saw the map, yet the swarm found the food.
Nobody saw the map, yet the swarm found the food.
In this run, each particle keeps only sixty percent of its old velocity. That extra setting is called w.
Here each particle keeps 60% of its old velocity.
At step seven the odour reaches ninety-seven. That is good enough.
Step 7: odour 97, a good enough answer.
By step nineteen the swarm has shrunk to almost a point.
Step 19: the swarm has shrunk to almost a point.
Then eight steps pass with no new best, and then the step limit.
Then 8 steps with no new best, then the step limit.
Any one of the four rules can end the run.
Any one of the four rules can end the run.
A bit is zero or one, so adding zero point seven makes no sense.
A bit is 0 or 1: adding 0.7 makes no sense.
Binary PSO keeps the velocity between zero and one.
Binary PSO keeps v between 0 and 1.
The two pulls add zero point two and zero point one, so v is now zero point eight.
The two pulls add 0.2 and 0.1: v is now 0.8.
A random draw of zero point five five is below zero point eight, so the bit becomes one.
Draw rand(): 0.55 is below 0.8, so the bit is 1.
So v is the chance of a one, drawn again every step.
